vulnerabilities.weakness: The single payment service replica can directly prevent revenue-generating checkout completion.
vulnerabilities.hypothesis: If the paymentservice pod is killed, then checkout payments fail and purchases cannot complete until it returns.

vulnerabilities.weakness: The single entrypoint has only one replica, so its failure can take the whole site offline.
vulnerabilities.hypothesis: If the frontend pod is killed, then users cannot reach the site until Kubernetes recreates it.

vulnerabilities.weakness: The checkout orchestrator has only one replica, so its failure can stop all purchases.
vulnerabilities.hypothesis: If the checkoutservice pod is killed, then frontend checkout requests fail until the pod is recreated.

vulnerabilities.weakness: The single cart datastore replica creates a checkout-path availability risk despite persistent storage.
vulnerabilities.hypothesis: If the redis-cart pod is killed, then cart reads or writes and checkout operations fail until the pod returns.

vulnerabilities.weakness: The single cart service replica is a checkout-path single point of failure.
vulnerabilities.hypothesis: If the cartservice pod is killed, then users cannot view or update carts and checkout requests depending on carts fail.

vulnerabilities.weakness: The single email service replica is synchronously or functionally exposed on the checkout path according to the dependency facts.
vulnerabilities.hypothesis: If the emailservice pod is killed, then checkout completion or its confirmation flow fails or stalls.

vulnerabilities.weakness: The single shipping service replica is a checkout-path single point of failure.
vulnerabilities.hypothesis: If the shippingservice pod is killed, then shipping selection or checkout requests that require shipping fail.

vulnerabilities.weakness: The optional advertising service has a single replica and is expected to fail gracefully without blocking checkout.
vulnerabilities.hypothesis: If the adservice pod is killed, then advertisements disappear or the frontend loses ad content while core browsing and checkout remain available.

systemic: Every service has pdb=false, so planned disruption or voluntary eviction can remove the only available pod for single-replica services.
Every service has hpa=false, so CPU saturation or traffic spikes cannot trigger automatic horizontal capacity.
Most services are single-replica dependencies; failures can cascade through the dependency graph even though readiness_probe and liveness_probe are enabled.
blind_spots: These facts cannot show request timeouts, retry behavior, circuit breakers, fallback handling, or whether checkout calls are synchronous.
They cannot show whether persistentVolumeClaim data is replicated, backed up, or recoverable after storage failure.
They cannot show pod scheduling across nodes or zones, topology spread, anti-affinity, or node-level failure impact.
They cannot show resource requests, actual utilization, throttling, queueing, or behavior under CPU or memory stress.
They cannot show whether the frontend and checkoutservice gracefully degrade when optional or downstream services fail.
